messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: R-4.2
parts:
We have moved to R-4.2 and there is a new version of today 22.05.07.
This is essentially the same as version 22.05.03 built with R-4.1.

Binary builds for Ubuntu-2204 is now available using
'inla.binary.install()'.

Best
H



--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org

messages.author: 94866edf3707c5ee
messages.subject: Re: R-4.2
parts:
I upgraded to R 4.2 on Fedora 35:

> INLA::inla.upgrade()
This is INLA_21.11.22 built 2021-11-21 16:10:15 UTC.
 - See www.r-inla.org/contact-us for how to get help.
 - To enable PARDISO sparse library; see inla.pardiso()
INLA :
 Version 21.11.22 installed in /home/rsb/lib/r_libs
 Version 22.05.07 available at https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable
Update? (Yes/no/cancel) yes

but now see:

> result = inla(formula, family = "gaussian", data = data)
/home/rsb/lib/r_libs/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/inla.mkl: /home/rsb/lib/r_libs/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/libcrypto.so.1.1: version `OPENSSL_1_1_1b' not found (required by /lib64/libk5crypto.so.3)
/home/rsb/lib/r_libs/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/inla.mkl: /home/rsb/lib/r_libs/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/libcrypto.so.1.1: version `OPENSSL_1_1_1b' not found (required by /lib64/libk5crypto.so.3)
Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() :
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.

Is there a known workaround, or should I try re-ordering the shared objects in /home/rsb/lib/r_libs/INLA/bin/linux/64bit ? Can MKL (if that is the BLAS being used) be avoided ?

Roger
